extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society; natural philosophers, experimenters, and seamen making scientific observations on voyages
extracted.subtask_description: A set of instructions and required observations for seamen on long voyages aimed at collecting scientific data (magnetic variation, tides, coasts, soundings, weather, meteors, sea-water samples, etc.) to support natural philosophy and mapmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the declination (variation) of the compass
rubrics_metrics.description: To observe the declination of the compass, or its variation from the meridian; noting also the latitude and longitude of the place where such observation is made, and stating the method of taking them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the place's latitude and longitude alongside the compass variation and explicitly state the method used to determine those coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry dipping needles and record inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: To carry dipping needles with them, and observe their inclination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring dipping needles as instruments and systematically measure and record magnetic inclination (dip) at observed locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe tides with full circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: To observe carefully the tides in as many places as they can, with all the circumstances; such as the precise time of ebbing and flowing in rivers, and at capes; the set of their currents, the perpendicular distance between the highest tide and lowest ebb, in spring and neap tides; what day of the moon's age, and what times of the year, the highest and lowest tides happen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each tidal observation record precise times, locations (rivers, capes), current set, vertical range (high to low), whether spring or neap, the moon's age at extremes, and season/time of year; capture as many different places as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make plots and draughts of coasts and features
rubrics_metrics.description: To make plots and draughts of coasts, promontories, islands and ports, marking the bearings and distances as near as may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce maps/drafts of coastal features indicating bearings and estimated distances; strive for as much accuracy as possible in plotting relative positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and mark depths of coasts and ports
rubrics_metrics.description: To sound and mark the depths of coasts, ports, and other places near the shore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take systematic depth soundings in coastal and port areas and annotate charts with measured depths for navigation and study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record nature of seabed in all soundings
rubrics_metrics.description: To observe, in all soundings, the nature of the ground at the bottom of the sea, whether it be clay, sand, rock, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sounding, collect or note the character of the seabed (clay, sand, rock, etc.) to accompany depth measurements—use for navigation, anchoring, and geological knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a register of wind and weather changes
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep a register of all changes of the wind and weather at all hours, both day and night, the point the wind blows from, and whether strong or weak; the rains, hail, snow, &c., the precise times of their beginnings and continuance, especially hurricanes and spouts; and above all, carefully to observe the trade-winds, about what degrees of latitude and longitude they first begin, where and when they cease, or change, or grow stronger or weaker, and how much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain continuous meteorological logs noting wind direction and strength, onset and duration of precipitation and severe events, and detailed tracking of trade-winds' latitudinal/longitudinal extents and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe extraordinary meteors and record specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: To observe all extraordinary meteors, lightnings, thunders, ignes fatui, comets, &c., marking the places and times of their appearing, continuance, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record occurrences of unusual atmospheric or astronomical phenomena with precise times, locations, durations, and any notable characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect sea-water samples and measure weight/salinity
rubrics_metrics.description: To carry with them good scales, and glass-vials of about a pint, with narrow mouths, to be filled with sea-water in different latitudes, in order to know its weight, both of the water near the surface and at greater depths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring appropriate vessels and scales to take sea-water samples at various latitudes and depths; measure and record weights (proxy for salinity/density) for comparative studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for measuring distances from one station with a large telescope
rubrics_metrics.description: A method of measuring, with a large telescope, from one station, the distance of objects on the earth; using an ordinary telescope with a convex eye-glass, adjusting the spacing of glasses proportionally to the distance, adding a new eye-glass so the object is seen distinct and erect; can be done by leaving the telescope in its ordinary situation (object-glass before the eye-glass) or inverting it; if two object-glasses with known foci are used their distance will be known and the focus of the second can be found by the given relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical notes: the theory doesn't fully account for telescope length variability; use convex eye-glass, adjust inter-glass spacing slightly greater than usual proportional to target distance, consider inverting telescope as alternative; use two object-glasses with known focal lengths and apply the provided focal-distance arithmetic to determine placement and achieve desired magnification. Expect some practical latitude but accuracy comparable to common instrument methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Way of preparing a liquor to penetrate and colour marble
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipe and procedure to prepare liquids that sink into and colour the whole body of marble so that a picture drawn on the surface appears in the inmost parts of the stone: use aqua fortis and aqua regia (two ounces each), sal ammoniac (one ounce), spirit of wine (two drams), gold (small amount), and silver (two drams); calcine metals and evaporate with acids to produce coloured waters; apply these waters repeatedly to soft white marble so the colour penetrates over days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed recipe steps are given (calcine silver and gold, treat with aqua fortis/regia, evaporate, prepare tinctures from other metals). Repeat application daily; depth of penetration depends on duration. The text also notes an alternative/prior method by Mr. Bird (stone-cutter) who applies a colour to polished marble that sinks to variable depths by continued application—practical verification available in specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of conveying liquors directly into the blood (intravenous injection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure ascribed to Dr. Christopher Wren: make a ligature on a vein, open the vein on the side of the ligature towards the heart, introduce slender syringes or quills fastened to bladders (like clyster pipes) containing the matter to be injected; performed on large lean dogs for accessible vessels; examples include injecting opium (stupifies but not fatal) and crocus metallorum (large dose caused vomiting and death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical notes: choose suitably large/lean animals for vessel access; effects of injected substances vary—record physiological outcomes. The account references Boyle's further, more circumstantial descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve ice and snow using chaff (insulation and drainage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction and practice at Leghorn: build snow/ice-houses as deep pits on a steep hill with drainage, thatch cover to prevent rain entrance; line bottom and sides thickly with chaff (barley chaff suggested), fill and ram down pure snow/ice, cover heavily. In six months they lose about one-eighth of weight; when removed, wrap in chaff to retain cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure pure water for stored ice used in wine; maintain drainage so meltwater does not stagnate; use thick chaff insulation on sides and top; when transporting or exposing blocks wrap in chaff for preservation. Alternative insulating materials: straw or reed also effective (see Boyle's Experimental History of Cold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational targets and considerations for lunar study
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for what lunar observers (those with good telescopes) should attend to: look for seasonal changes on Earth as seen from the Moon (different faces in seasons), rivers, fluxes, large ice masses, effects of cleared forests/drained marshes, volcanoes distinguishable in shadow, luminous fires in towns/forests during eclipses or non-illuminated portions; examine maps (Hevelius, Divini, Riccioli) for changes and discrepancies in clear and dark regions; consider whether lunar seas may be on the opposite hemisphere; note absence/presence of clouds, vapours, and twilight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious in asserting conclusions; compare repeated observations and maps for changes over time; use improved telescopes to seek faint lights beyond the terminator; recent telescope improvements (e.g., Herschel) have enabled verification of some speculations—observers encouraged to monitor and record any apparent changes.
